scope: Independent audit of the weighted channel-spectrum extension and its explicit12-state example; no unrestricted target proof or general coarse-monotonicity claim.
mathematical_audit: Original measure is pi on coarse states and pi_i/2 on each of two fine states. Symmetry and |H|<=S imply actual root nonnegativity, and averaging the sign b gives the Markov row sum without changing weights.
From H^2=beta Id+(alpha-beta)Pi one has H^(2n)=beta^n[t_n Id+(1-t_n)(Id-Pi)], t_n=(alpha/beta)^n. The beta=0 endpoint is separate and immediate.

The seven Eulerian K4 cycle contributions use original-pi composition and integration. The Id/P tables follow contraction of identity components and P=Id-Pi inclusion-exclusion; an identity tree leaves pi_i while an identity cycle adds r_i=1/pi_i.

For L=S^(2n), L=Pi+PSD centered remainder gives L(i,i)>=1 and trace L>=1. Products of two such common powers have trace>=1. The mean of V_i=E_j L_x L_y L_z is>=1 by Schur PSD expansion; no pointwise V_i>=1 is assumed.

The triangle and quadrilateral tables have the stated weighted r_i-j coefficients. With r_i>=d>=4, each coefficient used in the lower bound is nonnegative. Replacing it by d-j and using E V>=1 or D_i>=1 yields d-1 for every nonfull identity subset and d for the full identity cycle.
Mixture averaging therefore gives beta^q(d-1)+alpha^q. The coefficient is d-1=1/max(pi)-1 and is not the dimension of the centered coarse space.

For the six-state star, ordinary root eigenvalues are1,1953/2048 (multiplicity4),1701/2048 (multiplicity1). The odd channel contributes squared values1/16384 (multiplicity5) and0 (multiplicity1). Removing one fine constant eigenvalue leaves exactly four distinct values, including zero.

The coarse common-cone all-identity coefficient is sum pi_i^(-2)-1=299, giving the displayed1+299 y^N bound before the channel surplus. For this measure d-1=4 whereas the centered coarse dimension is5.
All off-diagonal entries of H^2 are negative, so their signs around any coarse triple have negative product and cannot be made all nonnegative by a diagonal sign gauge.
The theorem retains its weighted atom bound max pi<=1/4 and its channel-square spectral hypothesis. It makes no assertion for arbitrary H or arbitrary heavy atoms.
